findings.passage: “We are a nation of laws,” said Senate Majority Whip Steve Gooch, R-Dahlonega. “We’re used to having identification cards on us. “I just can’t understand anybody opposing requiring some kind of identification to present to an elections office to prove who you say you are.”
findings.note: Quoted by Capitol Beat in committee on Sen. Larry Walker's bill requiring a driver's license or other ID number to request an absentee ballot. He supports requiring identification for absentee ballot requests and compares it to showing ID in person.
subjects: ID to request a mail or absentee ballot

findings.passage: “We want every legal voter in Georgia to go vote. We’re not trying to suppress the vote. We’re not trying to keep Democrats from coming out to vote,” Gooch added.
findings.note: Quoted by Fetch Your News (White County meeting) on the Senate omnibus election bill; says the aim is for every legal voter to vote and not to suppress votes. The same article reports he backs a photo ID for absentee ballots (reporter's words, not saved as his).
subjects: ID with a mail or absentee ballot

findings.passage: Gooch stated, “I’m ready to get rid of all the drop boxes that was not allowed in state law, and it’s still not allowed in state law. That was done as an executive order by the Secretary of State under a national emergency powers act, and we’re going to close the loophole.”
findings.note: Quoted by Fetch Your News on ending absentee ballot drop boxes in the Senate omnibus election bill. Related election-integrity topic, tagged: drop boxes.
